established_findings.statement: Large language models and agentic/multi-agent frameworks are being actively applied to NetOps problems such as intent-to-configuration translation, automated configuration generation, and VNF/service deployment in experimental and prototype systems.
limitations: Evaluations are largely on curated or simulated setups and prototypes rather than broad production deployments.
Reported results vary by task, model, and evaluation protocol; not a uniform performance claim.

established_findings.statement: Generate–Verify–Repair (GVR) or closed-loop generate–validate–repair architectures (interposing deterministic/verifier or test layers between generation and acceptance) are proposed and shown in code and systems experiments to detect and reduce mechanically verifiable errors and to provide structured repair feedback to LLMs.
limitations: Demonstrations focus on code or constrained verification tasks; extension to full NetOps semantics (multi-protocol, multi-vendor, emergent runtime effects) is not proven in the cited records.
Reported gains concern classes of mechanically checkable defects; semantic/intent alignment failures can remain.

established_findings.statement: Controlled benchmarks and task suites for AIOps/NetOps show that current LLM-based agents have substantial limitations on realistic operational tasks: low end-to-end success on many scenarios, sensitivity to ticket wording or false-premise reports, and a non-trivial rate of wrong-but-plausible outputs that can trigger actions.
limitations: Benchmarks vary in scope and scoring methodology; some rely on LLM-based judges or simulated tool effects.
Coverage of vendor heterogeneity and production-scale topology is limited in the cited suites.

established_findings.statement: Tool-augmented orchestration strategies (verifier-guided recovery, self-healing orchestrators) demonstrably reduce silent or wrong-but-plausible failures and improve task success in controlled evaluations compared with naive retry-only or non-verifying baselines.
limitations: Reported improvements are from controlled benchmarks; gains depend on quality/coverage of available tools and validators.
Orchestration-level failures (time-outs, stale context, tool malfunctions) remain a practical concern.

established_findings.statement: Choices between retrieval-augmentation (RAG), fine-tuning, or hybrid adaptation materially affect factuality, refusal/guardrail behavior, and deployment trade-offs; recent reviews and measured frameworks recommend task-dependent, auditable selection between these approaches.
limitations: Most analyses are conceptual or based on limited production case studies; direct NetOps-specific longitudinal evidence is sparse in the supplied records.

unresolved_questions.statement: How comprehensive and operationally sufficient are existing deterministic network-verification tools when used as validators inside GVR pipelines for real-world, multi-protocol, multi-vendor NetOps tasks?
limitations: Cited works discuss GVR architectures and verifier-guided inference but do not provide comprehensive empirical coverage of full-scale, heterogeneous NetOps validator completeness.

unresolved_questions.statement: To what extent do verifier-guided pipelines catch or prevent semantic/intent-misalignment errors that are syntactically valid and pass mechanical checks (i.e., correct-by-structure but incorrect-by-intent configurations)?
limitations: Existing demonstrations emphasize mechanically verifiable defects; specific evaluations of semantic intent preservation across complex NetOps tasks are not present among the supplied records.

unresolved_questions.statement: How well do current benchmark outcomes (ITBench, FaulT-Bench, LogEval-style suites) generalize to production networks with larger scale, multi-vendor devices, and evolving operator workflows?
limitations: The cited benchmarks document limitations and controlled conditions; direct transfer studies to production environments are not included in the supplied records.

unresolved_questions.statement: What human-in-the-loop gating, audit-trace, and operator-trust designs best balance automation benefits against risk for LLM/agentic NetOps in operational settings?
limitations: Surveys and frameworks recommend traceability and evidence planes but concrete comparative trials of alternative human–agent gating strategies in NetOps are not present in the provided records.

candidate_gaps.statement: There is a need for standardized, public NetOps benchmarks that combine realistic topologies, authentic operator-ticket noise (including false-premise tickets), executable validators, and reproducible scoring to measure end-to-end agentic behavior.
limitations: Existing benchmark efforts address parts of this desideratum (ticket realism, log analysis, IT tasks) but no single curated, widely adopted NetOps benchmark meeting all listed criteria is present in the supplied records.

candidate_gaps.statement: Quantitative metrics and protocols to measure validator soundness, coverage, false-positive/false-negative rates, and operational impact when used as oracles inside GVR flows are underdeveloped and would materially improve trustworthiness evaluations.
limitations: The cited works motivate validator layers and auditable traces but do not deliver a standard validator-metric suite tailored to NetOps.

candidate_gaps.statement: Publicly usable corpora of real-world router/firewall/switch configurations that preserve operational fidelity while protecting sensitive information are limited; privacy-preserving sharing mechanisms and synthetic-but-faithful generation methods are needed to support reproducible research.
limitations: NetCloak and related work propose anonymization strategies, but broad public corpora with standardized anonymization and validation are not evident in the supplied records.

candidate_gaps.statement: Longitudinal evidence on maintenance costs, model drift, and the operational burden of RAG vs. fine-tuned vs. hybrid NetOps adaptation strategies is sparse in the supplied literature.
limitations: Frameworks and case studies discuss trade-offs, but multi-month or multi-release empirical comparisons in NetOps contexts are not included among the provided records.

excluded_claims: LLMs are currently production-ready to fully autonomously manage network configurations across diverse, multi-vendor production environments without human oversight.
Deterministic proof that a generate–verify–repair pipeline can guarantee zero-defect network changes in real-world NetOps (no such general proof is present in the supplied records).
A claim of superior performance of a specific LLM or agent across all NetOps tasks without experimental support in the supplied records.
Any empirical result or dataset produced before the autonomous run that is not contained in the supplied record list (pre-lock development artifacts are excluded).
